newsitem.title: ERITREA: Eritrea plans sale of 14 more companies.
newsitem.headline: Eritrea plans sale of 14 more companies.

text.p: The Eritrean government plans to sell an additional 14 companies in its privatisation process, bringing the total number of companies to be sold to 37, a senior government official said.

Tewolde Woldemikael, director of the National Agency for Supervision and Privatisation of Public Enterprises, told Reuters: "We are in the process of preparing profiles for the 14 companies. The profiles are now in draft form. Once they are prepared, we will announce the invitation to bid."
He did not say what method would be used in the sale. Authorities said in July they would sell 23 companies.

Of the 14, eight were what Tewolde called "major industries" -- Asmara Textile Factory, Mereb Textile Factory, Red Sea Tannery, Eritrean Metal Sheet Factory, Orota Metal Works, Asmara Brewery, Eritrean Cement Factory and Gash Cigarettes & Tobacco.
Tewolde declined to disclose turnover or profit figures for the companies. "Most of our enterprises are doing quite all right," he said in an interview late on Tuesday.

He said the profiles of the companies would contain the value and volume of sales for the last three years. He said the government hoped Eritreans living abroad would bid for them: "We have sent the information to all our embassies abroad."
Asked what whether the exiled Eritreans would be financially strong enough to participate in the bidding, Tewolde replied: "We don't know. But we are giving them the opportunity."
Tewolde said several foreign companies have shown interest in Eritrean industries.
"Companies from Scandinavia and the Middle East have contacted us and asked for more information," he said but gave no details.

In the process of privatising the total of 37 companies, studies will be made of the possibility of selling additional government-owned enterprises. Among these are the Commercial Bank of Eritrea and the National Insurance Corporation, he said.
Tewolde said there was a possibility the government would also sell the Salt Works of Massawa and Assab on the Red Sea coast.
